name: SurveySparrow
tagline: Conversational surveys, NPS, employee experience, and automation

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 75 responses/quarter; 3 active Classic surveys; 1 active CX survey; 10 questions/survey; 1 user; 1,000 contacts; 200 emails; 0 API calls/day.
tiers.notes: The live comparison table/card says 75 responses/quarter, while an official FAQ on the same pricing surface says 50 responses/month; the table/card figure is used.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 2,500 responses/year; 1 user; 100 Classic surveys; 1 CX survey; 10,000 contacts; 7,500 emails; 500 API calls/day.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 15,000 responses/year; 1 user; 1,000 Classic surveys; 1 CX survey; 20,000 contacts; 45,000 emails; 1,000 API calls/day.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 36,000 responses/year; 3 users; 1,000 Classic surveys; 1 CX survey; 200,000 contacts; 108,000 emails; 40 document credits; 1,000 API calls/day.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 3+ users with custom responses, contacts, emails, API limits, security and support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 75 responses/quarter; 3 active Classic surveys; 1 active CX survey; 10 questions/survey; 1 user; 1,000 contacts; 200 emails; 0 API calls/day. An official FAQ conflicts by stating 50 responses/month.
pricing.billingTerms: Quarterly + annual; the public card checked exposed annual-equivalent prices but not exact quarterly charges.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Additional users cost $49/user/month; extra response/API capacity is quote-based; purchased extra responses expire rather than rolling indefinitely; subscriptions auto-renew.

verdictSummary: The visible experience surveys loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. SurveySparrow earns its keep through delivery, integrations, compliance, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a experience surveys tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: SMTP or transactional email key in .env
whatYouLose: spam and abuse defense at scale
whyPeopleStillPay: SurveySparrow: Customers pay for dependable collection, spam control, notifications, integrations, and confidence that responses will not disappear.
ongoingBurden: Own storage, webhooks, email delivery, spam, file uploads, privacy requests, schema changes, and uptime.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of SurveySparrow is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for SurveySparrow, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a experience surveys tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: enterprise workflow logic; spam and abuse defense at scale; large integration and template catalog.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
